{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"d15dc7390d9c52e0145fb448d17e4ef18bc1fb6e2240dc8f414c53f0dba155ff","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:32","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Parking and stopping: parallel, angle and hill parking, disabled parking, no-parking places and distances, emergency parking","heading":"C — Parking and stopping: leaving a parked spot, parallel and angle parking, wheel position on hills, disabled parking spaces, where you may never stop or park, and emergency parking","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Parking and stopping: leaving a parked spot, parallel and angle parking, wheel position on hills, disabled parking spaces, where you may never stop or park, and emergency parking
Knowledge domain: how to pull out of and into parking spaces, how to set the wheels and brake on a hill, the disabled parking rules, the full list of places and distances where stopping or parking is banned, and what to do when a breakdown forces you to stop.

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
When you pull out from a parked or stopped position, check your mirrors and blind spots and yield to all other traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
When parallel parking, face the same direction that traffic moves in that lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Park parallel to the curb and no more than 12 inches from it, or if there is no curb, as close as you can to the edge of the shoulder. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Where parking spaces are marked, your wheels must be inside the marked space. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
The manual's parallel parking steps are to pull even with the car labeled Car A, back slowly into the space while turning the wheels sharply, and then straighten the wheels. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
Angle parking is common in parking lots, at shopping centers and on wide streets. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
When driving a large vehicle, avoid angle spaces where your vehicle would stick out and block traffic on the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
Signs may show that an angle parking area is reverse angle or back-in only. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A02
When parking on a hill, always set the parking brake, and leave a manual transmission in gear or an automatic transmission in park. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
On a hill, turn your front wheels so the vehicle would not roll downhill into traffic if the brake failed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A02
Parked downhill next to a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A02
Parked uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels toward the travel lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A02
Parked on a hill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
Oregon issues special parking permits to people with disabilities and to groups that transport people with disabilities. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
A disabled parking space may show the disability symbol painted on the ground as well as a sign with the symbol at the front of the space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
Parking in a space marked for people with disabilities is illegal unless you have a valid disabled parking permit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A03
Parking in a disabled space without a Disabled Person Parking Permit brings fines that start at $165 and can reach $1,000, even if you park there only a few minutes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A03
Parking and stopping rules apply whether or not you are inside the vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A03
The no-stopping and no-parking places do not apply when your vehicle breaks down and cannot be moved out of the traffic lanes, or when the shoulder has no room for you to pull off. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A03
You may not stop or park in a traffic lane of a highway, street or road, or inside an intersection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A03
Double parking, which means stopping on the road side of a vehicle that is already parked, is not allowed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A03
You may not stop or park on a sidewalk, crosswalk, bicycle lane or path, or on any railroad or light rail tracks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A03
You may not stop or park on a bridge or overpass, in a tunnel, or between the separate roadways of a divided highway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A03
You may not stop or park near construction or road work where your vehicle would interfere with traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A03
You may not stop or park in front of a public or private driveway, or anywhere that official signs, traffic control devices, diagonal stripes or other road markings forbid it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A03
You may not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A04
You may not park within 15 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side of the street, or within 75 feet of it on the opposite side. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A04
You may not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A04
You may not park within 50 feet of a traffic signal or sign if your vehicle would hide it from view. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A04
At a railroad or light rail crossing, keep your parked vehicle at least 50 feet from the closest rail. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A04
You may not park within 7 1/2 feet of railroad or light rail tracks when your vehicle would interfere with a train. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A04
If your vehicle breaks down and there is no other choice, you may stop or park for a short time where it is normally banned, as long as it creates no hazard, and you turn on your hazard lights. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A04
When needed, you may park on a highway shoulder if passing traffic still has enough room to get by. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A04
If your stopped vehicle cannot be seen from 200 feet away in each direction, warn oncoming drivers using flags, flares, signs, signals or flaggers set out at least 200 feet from the vehicle in both directions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A04
Before leaving a vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, take out the key, set the brakes and switch on the hazard lights. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A04
A police officer may have a vehicle removed if it is parked where parking is banned or creates a hazard, and the owner pays the towing and storage costs. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

Misconceptions: a quick stop in a disabled space is still illegal and still fined; the no-parking list applies even if you stay in the car; uphill with a curb the wheels turn away from the curb, not toward it; the hydrant, crosswalk, signal and railroad distances are different numbers, not one shared distance; a breakdown lets you stop in a banned place only for a short time and only without creating a hazard.
Mnemonics: down to the curb, up to the lane, no curb to the edge; brake set and in park or gear on every hill; engine off, key out, brakes on, flashers on before you walk away.
Glossary: parallel parking means parking in line with the curb in the direction of traffic; angle parking means parking at a slant to the curb or aisle; double parking means stopping on the road side of a parked vehicle; Disabled Person Parking Permit means the Oregon permit that allows parking in disabled spaces; hazard lights means the flashers that warn other drivers of a stopped vehicle.
Dynamic facts: the disabled parking fine range is a money amount that can change with law, so it is shown as printed in the current manual and re-checked each edition.
